page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the N2 instance family. It is equipped with 4 dedicated virtual CPUs backed by 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set features include AVX, AVX-512, AES, BMI2, and FMA. This instance has no attached local storage and contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations show distinct performance traits across compute and memory vectors. Compute-heavy operations record lower output, evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1404.38 and a multi-core score of 3680.85. Multi-core Geekbench tests yield 2492.0, while PassMark CPU scoring registers at 4320.42. In memory bandwidth testing, uncached 256MB read bandwidth reaches 26.28 GB/sec, and write bandwidth measures 22.5 GB/sec. PassMark memory testing achieves an average rating with a score of 2173.39, and single-threaded gzip compression performs in the middle tier at 23.92 GB/sec. Database benchmark operations report Redis SET handling reaching 3.61 million operations per second.

The resource profile of the n2-highmem-4 trades raw CPU processing power for elevated RAM capacity per core. For compute-bound tasks or complex parallel calculations, the lower virtual core count creates processing bottlenecks. However, the qualitative cost efficiency of this configuration is suited for memory-bound workloads that do not require heavy concurrent compute. Recommended application fits include in-memory caching layers, moderate-scale relational databases, microservices with high memory footprints, and data processing routines reliant on RAM allocation rather than high CPU core density.
